title: Abelian model recognition from small cotorsion pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in a fixed universe. Let $\mathcal Q,\mathcal W,\mathcal F$ be classes of its objects. A class is thick if it is closed under retracts and, in a short exact sequence, membership of any two objects implies membership of the third. For classes $\mathcal L,\mathcal T$, a cotorsion pair means $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal L^{\perp_1}$, where $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits. It is complete if each $X$ occurs in exact sequences $0\to T\to L\to X\to0$ and $0\to X\to T'\to L'\to0$ with the indicated terms in the two classes. It is small if a set $I$ of monomorphisms with cokernels in $\mathcal L$ has as its right lifting class exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$; a lifting class consists of maps against which every commutative square has a diagonal filler.

Suppose $\mathcal W$ is thick and $(\mathcal Q,\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W)$ and $(\mathcal Q\cap\mathcal W,\mathcal F)$ are complete small cotorsion pairs. There is a combinatorial abelian model structure on $\mathcal B$. Its cofibrations are precisely the monomorphisms with cokernel in $\mathcal Q$, its trivial cofibrations are those with cokernel in $\mathcal Q\cap\mathcal W$, its fibrations are precisely the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal F$, and its trivial fibrations are those with kernel in $\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W$. A morphism is a weak equivalence precisely when it factors as a trivial cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. Combinatorial here includes that $\mathcal B$ is locally presentable (cocomplete and generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a set of sufficiently presentable objects), the two weak factorization systems are generated by sets, and both factorizations can be chosen functorially. A model structure means these two weak factorization systems, weak equivalences closed under retracts and satisfying two-out-of-three, and all small limits and colimits. A weak factorization system $(L,T)$ means every map factors as a map in $L$ followed by a map in $T$, and $L$ and $T$ are exactly each other's left and right lifting classes.
